Eight public service workers set out carrying fully paid travel rations and radio equipment. After 600 seconds, they will verify the local population against the world's original ledger; unvisited regions remain unknown.
Joint clearing is now active: trade goods are physically withdrawn from storage and shipped, and the sum of all regions' credit and debt always equals zero.

The trade, transit, and supply-and-demand conventions are fully paid for and active; from now on, alliance upkeep, trade route freight costs, and payment for goods are all paid directly from the public budget.

Three-party multilateral negotiations are now active; each nation will weigh its raw material dependence, old debts on the books, and wartime losses, then vote independently on whether to stay or leave.
Postwar negotiations have been established; but a ceasefire on paper will not revive the fallen, conjure up depleted building materials, or erase old debts.
